places.name: Copenhagen
places.summary: Denmark's capital, a compact, flat and very bikeable city of canals, royal palaces, design shops and excellent museums. Easily the best base for the east of the country, with fast trains to Helsingør, Roskilde and the airport.
facts: The Copenhagen Card (24–120 h) covers public transport in the capital region and free entry to ~80 sights; it pays off with 3+ paid sights a day
Don't drive in the centre: street parking is expensive and limited; park at a suburban station and take the S-train or metro
Rent a city bike or regular bike: cycling is the local way to get around
Metro from the airport to the centre takes about 15 minutes

places.name: Tivoli Gardens
places.summary: One of the world's oldest amusement parks (1843), right in the city centre: gardens, historic rides, a pantomime theatre and thousands of lights after dark. Atmospheric rather than thrilling, and at its best in the evening.
facts: Entry roughly 160–190 DKK, rides extra (or an unlimited ride pass); entry is included in the Copenhagen Card
Book ahead on summer weekends and for Friday Rock concerts
Seasonal: summer season plus Halloween and Christmas markets; closed for some weeks in winter and spring
Go late afternoon and stay for the lights

places.name: Nyhavn
places.summary: The postcard 17th-century canal lined with brightly painted townhouses and old wooden ships. Touristy and pricey to eat at, but a must for a stroll and the starting point of most canal tours.
facts: Free to walk; restaurants on the sunny north side are expensive, buy a drink and sit on the quay instead
Hans Christian Andersen lived at numbers 18, 20 and 67
Best light in the morning and early evening

places.name: Copenhagen canal tour
places.summary: A one-hour open-boat tour from Nyhavn or Gammel Strand through the harbour and Christianshavn's canals, passing the Opera House, the Little Mermaid and Christiansborg. A quick, relaxing way to get your bearings.
facts: Around 100–130 DKK; the classic Nyhavn tour is included in the Copenhagen Card
Departures every 30–60 minutes in season, fewer in winter
Sit on the outside edge for photos and bring a layer: it is windy on the water
places.season: Boats run all year but the open boats are most pleasant May–September.

places.name: Christiansborg Palace
places.summary: Seat of the Danish parliament, Supreme Court and the royal reception rooms, on the island of Slotsholmen. Visit the lavish reception rooms with the modern tapestries of Danish history, the medieval ruins beneath and the royal stables.
facts: Combined ticket around 175 DKK; free with the Copenhagen Card
The tower (Tårnet) has free entry and one of the best views over the city — expect a short queue
Reception rooms can close at short notice for royal events
Parliament (Folketinget) offers free guided tours on some days

places.name: Rosenborg Castle
places.summary: Christian IV's Renaissance castle from the early 1600s, with original royal interiors and, in the basement treasury, the Danish crown jewels. Set in the King's Garden, the city's oldest park.
facts: ~140 DKK; free with the Copenhagen Card
Book a time slot online in summer, when the narrow rooms get crowded
Allow 1–1.5 hours; the King's Garden around it is free

places.name: Amalienborg & the Marble Church
places.summary: The royal family's winter residence: four identical rococo palaces around an octagonal square, facing the domed Marble Church (Frederik's Church). The Changing of the Guard marches into the square at noon.
facts: The square and guard change (daily, 12:00) are free; the Amalienborg Museum is ticketed and included in the Copenhagen Card
The Marble Church is free to enter; the dome can be climbed on guided tours
Combine with a walk along the harbour to the Opera House view and the Little Mermaid

places.name: National Museum of Denmark
places.summary: Denmark's main museum of history, from Bronze Age lurs and the Sun Chariot to Viking finds and everyday life through the centuries. The prehistory galleries are the highlight.
facts: ~130 DKK; free with the Copenhagen Card, under-18s free
Big: pick the prehistory and Viking sections if short of time
Good rainy-day option a few minutes from Tivoli

places.name: National Gallery of Denmark (SMK)
places.summary: The national art museum, with the Danish Golden Age painters, the Skagen painters, Old Masters and a strong modern collection, in a historic building joined to a bright modern extension.
facts: ~140 DKK; free with the Copenhagen Card, under-27s discounted, under-18s free
Open late on Wednesday evenings
Next to the Botanical Garden and Rosenborg, so easy to combine

places.name: Ny Carlsberg Glyptotek
places.summary: The Carlsberg brewer's art collection: Egyptian, Greek and Roman sculpture, French Impressionists and Rodin, around a palm-filled winter garden café. Beautiful building, never too crowded.
facts: ~125 DKK; free with the Copenhagen Card
The winter garden café is a pleasant stop even on a short visit
Opposite Tivoli and the main station

places.name: Round Tower (Rundetaarn)
places.summary: A 17th-century observatory tower with a wide spiral ramp instead of stairs, leading to a platform with views over the old city's roofs and spires.
facts: ~40 DKK; free with the Copenhagen Card
Allow 30 minutes; the ramp is easy for all ages
In the Latin Quarter, near the Strøget shopping street

places.name: Church of Our Saviour
places.summary: A baroque church in Christianshavn whose black-and-gold corkscrew spire has an external staircase winding to the top, with a dizzying view over the city. Inside is a huge carved organ held up by elephants.
facts: The church is free; climbing the spire is ticketed and timed — book online in summer
Over 400 steps, the last ones narrow and outside; not for those with vertigo
The spire closes in strong wind, rain or ice
places.caution: The final section of the spire is steep, narrow and exposed to the wind.

places.name: Freetown Christiania
places.summary: A self-governing hippie commune founded in 1971 in former barracks in Christianshavn, with self-built houses, murals, workshops, cafés and lakeside paths. Its quieter residential corners are the most interesting part.
facts: Free to walk around; residents offer guided tours
Don't take photos around the former Pusher Street area
Walk out to the lakeside paths on the ramparts behind the main area
places.caution: Cannabis dealing (illegal in Denmark) has led to police raids and violence around Pusher Street; respect the no-photo rule and stay alert there.

places.name: The Little Mermaid & Kastellet
places.summary: The small bronze statue (1913) based on Andersen's fairy tale sits on a rock off the Langelinie promenade. Famously underwhelming on its own, but worth it combined with the star-shaped Kastellet fortress next door and the Gefion Fountain.
facts: Free; crowded with tour groups from mid-morning, go early or in the evening
Kastellet's ramparts make a free, pleasant loop walk
About a 20-minute walk north of Nyhavn along the harbour

places.name: Torvehallerne food market
places.summary: Two glass market halls by Nørreport station with around 60 stalls: smørrebrød, fish, coffee, pastries and Danish produce. A good lunch stop.
facts: Free entry; lunch roughly 100–150 DKK
Busy at weekday lunchtime and Saturday morning
Shorter hours on Sunday

places.name: The Blue Planet (National Aquarium)
places.summary: Northern Europe's largest aquarium, in a striking swirl-shaped building on the Amager coast near the airport, with a large ocean tank with hammerhead sharks and a tropical rainforest hall.
facts: Included in the Copenhagen Card; book a time slot online on weekends and school holidays
Metro to Kastrup station, then a short walk
Good with children and on rainy days

places.name: Amager Strandpark
places.summary: A long artificial sandy beach and lagoon a few metro stops from the centre, with the Kastrup Sea Bath's round wooden pier nearby. Where Copenhageners swim in summer.
facts: Free; metro M2 to Amager Strand or Femøren
Water quality is monitored and usually good
Busy on warm summer weekends
places.season: Swimming is realistic from late June to August; the water rarely exceeds 20 °C.

places.name: Dragør
places.summary: A well-preserved 18th-century skipper's village at the southern tip of Amager, with yellow houses, cobbled lanes, hollyhocks and a small harbour. A quiet contrast to the city, 15 minutes from the airport.
facts: Bus 350S from the centre or a short drive from the airport
Free parking by the harbour outside peak summer
Good fish restaurants and an ice-cream stop at the harbour

places.name: Dyrehaven deer park & Eremitage
places.summary: A UNESCO-listed royal hunting forest north of the city, with ancient oaks, open grassland and around 2,000 free-roaming red and fallow deer around the Eremitage hunting lodge.
facts: Free; S-train to Klampenborg, then walk in
Rent a bike or take a horse carriage ride from the entrance
Deer are easiest to see early morning and towards dusk
Combine with Bakken amusement park and Bellevue beach next to the station

places.name: Bakken (Dyrehavsbakken)
places.summary: The world's oldest operating amusement park, in the edge of Dyrehaven forest: old-fashioned, folksy and cheaper than Tivoli, with a wooden roller coaster from 1932.
facts: Free entry; pay per ride or buy a wristband
Seasonal, roughly late March to the end of August, plus Halloween and Christmas events
10 minutes' walk from Klampenborg S-train station

places.name: Helsingør
places.summary: A historic port town facing Sweden across the narrow Øresund, home to Kronborg Castle, a medieval old town with a Carmelite monastery and the excellent underground Maritime Museum.
facts: 45 minutes by train from Copenhagen; trains run every 20 minutes
Ferries to Helsingborg in Sweden every 20 minutes (20-minute crossing)
The Culture Yard (Kulturværftet) by the harbour has a café with castle views

places.name: Kronborg Castle
places.summary: The Renaissance castle guarding the Øresund, which once collected the Sound Dues and is the setting of Shakespeare's Hamlet. See the great ballroom, royal chambers and the dark casemates with the statue of Holger the Dane.
facts: ~150 DKK; free with the Copenhagen Card
Hamlet scenes are acted in the castle in summer
Bring a torch (or phone light) for the casemates
Allow 2–3 hours with the Maritime Museum next door

places.name: M/S Maritime Museum of Denmark
places.summary: A museum of Danish seafaring built underground in an old dry dock beside Kronborg, designed by BIG. The architecture is as much a draw as the ship models, tattoos and container-shipping story.
facts: ~150 DKK; free with the Copenhagen Card; combination tickets with Kronborg are cheaper
Allow 1–1.5 hours
The dry-dock bridges are free to walk over for a look

places.name: Louisiana Museum of Modern Art
places.summary: One of Europe's finest modern art museums, in low glass pavilions linked by corridors through a sculpture park running down to the Øresund. Strong temporary exhibitions plus Giacometti, Henry Moore and Yayoi Kusama.
facts: ~150–175 DKK; free with the Copenhagen Card
Train to Humlebæk, then a 10-minute walk
The café terrace and lawn above the sea are part of the experience
Open until 22:00 Tuesday–Friday

places.name: Karen Blixen Museum (Rungstedlund)
places.summary: The home of the author of Out of Africa, kept as she left it, with her flower arrangements, Kenyan mementos and a bird sanctuary garden where she is buried.
facts: ~100 DKK; free with the Copenhagen Card
Short walk from Rungsted Kyst station on the coast line
Usually closed on Mondays; shorter hours in winter

places.name: Hillerød
places.summary: A small town built around Frederiksborg Castle and its lake, at the centre of North Zealand's forests and lakes. A convenient base by car for the castles and beaches.
facts: 40 minutes from Copenhagen by S-train (line A, covered by the Copenhagen Card)
Local trains continue to Gilleleje, Tisvildeleje and Helsingør
Parking near the castle lake is easy outside summer weekends

places.name: Frederiksborg Castle
places.summary: Scandinavia's largest Renaissance castle, built by Christian IV on three islands in a lake. Inside is the Museum of National History with portraits and lavish rooms, including the magnificent chapel; outside are formal baroque gardens.
facts: ~120 DKK; free with the Copenhagen Card
The baroque gardens are free and open all day
Allow 2–3 hours; the chapel and the Great Hall are the highlights
Summer boat across the lake from the town
places.season: Longer opening hours (around 10:00–17:00) from April to October.

places.name: Fredensborg Palace Gardens
places.summary: The royal family's spring and autumn residence, an 18th-century baroque palace by Esrum Lake. The large park with avenues and the Norwegian sculpture garden is open to the public all year.
facts: The park is free; the palace interior opens only for guided tours in July
Changing of the Guard at noon when the King is in residence
Combine with a walk along Esrum Lake

places.name: Esrum Lake
places.summary: Denmark's second-largest lake, ringed by beech forest (Gribskov), with paths along the shore and summer boat trips. Quiet, green countryside between Hillerød and the coast.
facts: Free; parking at the Fredensborg and Sørup ends
Summer boat service crosses the lake
Gribskov forest to the west has marked walking and cycling trails

places.name: Hornbæk
places.summary: An old fishing village turned upmarket summer resort, with one of Zealand's best wide sandy beaches backed by dunes and pine plantation, and a small harbour.
facts: Free beach; paid parking in summer
Train from Helsingør on the coastal line
Hornbæk Plantage forest behind the beach has walking paths
places.season: Lively in July and August, very quiet out of season.

places.name: Gilleleje
places.summary: Zealand's northernmost fishing port, with a working harbour, fish smokehouses, thatched cottages and a cliff-top path past a Kierkegaard memorial stone.
facts: Buy fresh or smoked fish straight from the harbour
Coastal path east to Nakkehoved Lighthouse (about 2 km)
End of the local train line from Hillerød

places.name: Tisvildeleje & Tisvilde Hegn
places.summary: A small resort with a long sandy beach and a large pine and heath forest (Tisvilde Hegn) with wind-shaped trees and inland dunes. Popular with Copenhageners for summer weekends.
facts: Free beach; train from Hillerød to the end of the line
Walk to Troldeskoven (the Troll Forest) of twisted trees in Tisvilde Hegn
Sunsets over the Kattegat are a highlight

places.name: Arken Museum of Contemporary Art
places.summary: A ship-like museum on the beach at Ishøj, south-west of Copenhagen, with contemporary art exhibitions and works by Damien Hirst, Olafur Eliasson and others. Combine with the Ishøj beach park.
facts: Free with the Copenhagen Card
S-train to Ishøj, then bus or a 20-minute walk
Usually closed on Mondays

places.name: Roskilde
places.summary: Denmark's medieval royal and church capital at the head of the Roskilde Fjord, with its UNESCO cathedral and the Viking Ship Museum. A short train ride from Copenhagen and a good alternative base.
facts: About 25 minutes by train from Copenhagen
The Roskilde Festival (late June/early July) fills every bed in the area
Saturday market on the Stændertorvet square

places.name: Roskilde Cathedral
places.summary: The first Gothic brick cathedral in Scandinavia and the burial place of nearly 40 Danish kings and queens, whose tombs and chapels span 800 years of styles. A UNESCO World Heritage Site.
facts: Small entry fee; closed to visitors during services, weddings and funerals
Allow about 1 hour; the Christian IV chapel is the highlight
Shorter hours on Sundays

places.name: Viking Ship Museum
places.summary: Five original Viking ships, deliberately sunk around 1070 to block the fjord, displayed in a hall facing the water, with a boatyard building reconstructions. In summer you can row a replica Viking boat on the fjord.
facts: Adult ticket around 160–180 DKK; check whether it is included in your Copenhagen Card version
Summer sailing trips in replica ships are booked on the day at the museum
Check the museum website before going: a major rebuild of the ship hall is planned for the mid-2020s
15 minutes' walk downhill from the cathedral

places.name: Land of Legends (Sagnlandet Lejre)
places.summary: An open-air experimental archaeology park with reconstructed Stone Age, Iron Age and Viking settlements where volunteers live as in the past in summer. Nearby the Lejre Museum covers the legendary royal seat of Beowulf's Skjöldungs.
facts: Open roughly May–October; best in summer school holidays when the villages are inhabited
Lots of hands-on activities for children
Wear sturdy shoes: the site is large and partly in woods and fields

places.name: Køge
places.summary: A medieval market town with one of Denmark's best-preserved old centres of half-timbered houses around a large square. Also the port for the overnight ferry to Bornholm.
facts: S-train from Copenhagen (about 40 minutes)
Bornholmslinjen ferries to Rønne leave from Køge harbour
The KØS museum of art in public spaces is small and free

places.name: Stevns Klint
places.summary: A 15 km chalk and limestone cliff whose layers record the meteorite impact that ended the dinosaurs, now a UNESCO World Heritage Site. At Højerup the old church hangs over the edge after its choir fell into the sea in 1928.
facts: Free; parking at Højerup Old Church, which has a small visitor centre
Steps lead down to the beach where you can see the dark 'fish clay' boundary layer
Stevnsfort, a Cold War fortress inside the cliff, offers guided tours
places.caution: Keep away from the cliff edge and the base after rain: the chalk falls without warning.

places.name: Stege
places.summary: The main town of the island of Møn, with a medieval gate (Mølleporten) and remnants of its town ramparts. A small, practical base for Møns Klint and the island's frescoed churches.
facts: Supermarkets and fuel here before heading east to the cliffs
Møn is linked by bridge to Zealand; no ferry needed
Accommodation is limited: book ahead in summer

places.name: Møns Klint
places.summary: Spectacular white chalk cliffs rising 120 metres above a turquoise Baltic, topped by beech forest. Walk the clifftop paths and descend one of the long wooden staircases to the pebble beach, where fossils are common.
facts: The GeoCenter Møns Klint museum explains the geology (ticketed, open most of the year)
Parking is paid; the main staircase has around 500 steps
Allow at least 3 hours for a beach-and-clifftop loop
A designated dark-sky area: excellent stargazing on clear nights
places.caution: Cliff falls happen regularly; follow closures and do not walk directly under the cliff face.

places.name: Liselund
places.summary: A romantic late-18th-century landscape park near the cliffs of Møn, with a thatched little 'palace', a Swiss cottage and a Chinese tea house amid streams and lakes.
facts: The park is free; the small palace opens for short guided tours in summer
A few minutes' drive north of Møns Klint
Lovely in spring with the wild garlic and anemones

places.name: Fanefjord Church
places.summary: A white country church on western Møn whose vaults are covered with some of Denmark's finest late-medieval frescoes by the anonymous 'Elmelunde Master'.
facts: Free; usually open in daytime
Elmelunde and Keldby churches have frescoes by the same master
Short stop on the way between Stege and Bogø

places.name: Goose Tower, Vordingborg
places.summary: The best-preserved medieval tower in Denmark, crowned with a golden goose, standing among the ruins of Valdemar Atterdag's royal castle. The Danish Castle Centre (Danmarks Borgcenter) beside it tells the story.
facts: The ruins are free to walk; the museum and tower climb are ticketed
On the way from Zealand to Møn or Falster
Allow about an hour for the ruins, tower and museum

places.name: Nykøbing Falster
places.summary: The main town of Falster and Lolland, on the strait between them, with a medieval monastery church and the Middelaldercentret medieval experience centre nearby. A practical base for Knuthenborg and the Marielyst beaches.
facts: Main-line trains to Copenhagen (about 1 h 20 min)
Middelaldercentret, with a working trebuchet, is just outside town (summer season)
The Great Storstrøm Bridge (2022) links Falster to Zealand via Masnedø

places.name: Knuthenborg Safari Park
places.summary: Northern Europe's largest safari park, in the grounds of a manor on Lolland: drive among giraffes, rhinos, zebras and antelopes, then walk to the tigers and the big children's play areas.
facts: Open roughly late April to October; buy tickets online
You drive your own car through the safari section
Allow most of a day with children

places.name: Marielyst
places.summary: A long, fine sandy beach on the east coast of Falster, one of Denmark's sunniest spots and a classic family summer-house resort.
facts: Free beach with lifeguards in high summer
Shallow water, good for children
Busy with German and Danish holidaymakers in July

places.name: Sorø Abbey Church
places.summary: A 12th-century Cistercian church, one of the largest and oldest brick buildings in Denmark, with the tomb of Bishop Absalon, founder of Copenhagen. The pretty town sits on a lake.
facts: Free entry to the church
Walk around Sorø Lake or rent a boat in summer
Just off the E20 between Copenhagen and Funen

places.name: Trelleborg Viking Fortress
places.summary: The best-preserved of Harald Bluetooth's circular Viking fortresses (c. 980), part of a UNESCO World Heritage listing. The perfectly geometric earth rampart is free to walk; a museum and reconstructed longhouse explain it.
facts: Ramparts free; museum ticketed, with Viking activities in summer
Near Slagelse, a short detour from the motorway to Funen
Best seen from the top of the rampart

places.name: Odense
places.summary: Denmark's third city and the birthplace of Hans Christian Andersen, with a cobbled old quarter, a lively centre and good museums. The natural base for Funen.
facts: Driving from Zealand crosses the Great Belt Bridge (Storebælt): toll around 300 DKK per car each way, paid at the toll plaza
Intercity trains to Copenhagen take about 1 h 15 min
Light rail and buses connect the centre with the suburbs

places.name: H.C. Andersen's House
places.summary: A new (2021) museum by Kengo Kuma, partly underground, that brings Andersen's life and fairy tales to life through immersive rooms rather than display cases, linked to his birthplace and a fairy-tale garden.
facts: ~165 DKK; book a timed ticket online in summer
Allow about 2 hours; the children's section (Ludwig's Land) is separate
Andersen's childhood home on Munkemøllestræde is a short walk away

places.name: St Canute's Cathedral
places.summary: Denmark's finest Gothic brick church, with a gilded altarpiece and, in the crypt, the bones of King Canute IV, murdered here in 1086.
facts: Free entry
Next to the city park and the Andersen quarter
Allow 20–30 minutes; open daily outside services

places.name: The Funen Village (Den Fynske Landsby)
places.summary: An open-air museum of 18th- and 19th-century farmhouses, a mill and a smithy moved from around Funen, with animals and costumed demonstrations in summer.
facts: Main season roughly April–October
Summer boats along the Odense river from the city centre
Good with children

places.name: Egeskov Castle
places.summary: Europe's best-preserved Renaissance water castle (1554), standing in a lake on oak piles, with large gardens, mazes, a treetop walk and museums of vintage cars, motorcycles and aircraft.
facts: Pricey all-in ticket, but it fills most of a day
Open roughly May to October; the castle interior has shorter hours than the park
Between Odense and Svendborg; plenty of free parking

places.name: Svendborg
places.summary: A busy harbour town on the strait facing Tåsinge, the gateway to the South Funen Archipelago with ferries to Ærø and the small islands. Old wooden ships and harbour cafés.
facts: Ferries to Ærøskøbing (about 75 minutes) and to Skarø, Hjortø and Drejø
Summer veteran steamer Helge runs to Troense and Valdemars Slot
Regional trains from Odense take about 1 hour

places.name: Valdemars Castle
places.summary: A 17th-century manor built by Christian IV for his son, on Tåsinge across the strait from Svendborg, with furnished rooms, a hunting museum and a small beach.
facts: Open in the summer season only
Reach it by car over the bridge or by the summer steamer from Svendborg
The village of Troense nearby is one of Denmark's prettiest

places.name: Faaborg
places.summary: A charming small port with cobbled streets, a bell tower and the Faaborg Museum of Funen painters in a 1915 neoclassical building. Base for the hilly Svanninge Bakker and ferries to Avernakø and Lyø.
facts: Faaborg Museum is small and very fine (ticketed, closed Mondays in winter)
Ferries to the small islands of Lyø, Avernakø and Bjørnø
Svanninge Bakker hills are 10 minutes north for a short hike

places.name: Ærøskøbing (Ærø)
places.summary: A perfectly preserved 18th-century merchant town on the island of Ærø, with crooked cobbled lanes, painted half-timbered houses and hollyhocks. Ærø itself is gentle cycling country with beach huts and quiet beaches.
facts: Ferry from Svendborg takes about 75 minutes; book a car slot ahead in summer
Go as a foot passenger and rent a bike: the island is small
The Bottle Ship Museum (Flaskeskibssamlingen) is a quirky stop

places.name: Nyborg Castle
places.summary: Scandinavia's oldest royal castle (c. 1170), where Denmark's first constitution was signed in 1282. Reopened in 2023 after a major restoration and extension.
facts: Ticketed; closed Mondays outside summer
First town on Funen after the Great Belt Bridge (toll ~300 DKK by car)
The old town with its ramparts is pleasant for a short walk

places.name: Kerteminde
places.summary: A pretty fishing town on the Great Belt with a marina, old streets and Fjord & Bælt, where you can watch harbour porpoises being studied up close.
facts: Fjord & Bælt marine centre is good with children
Johannes Larsen Museum shows the Funen painter's home and garden
The Ladby Viking ship is 5 minutes' drive away

places.name: Ladby Viking Ship
places.summary: Denmark's only Viking ship burial, the imprint of a 10th-century chieftain's 21-metre ship preserved under a mound, with a small museum and a reconstruction.
facts: Ticketed; small site, 30–45 minutes is enough
Short drive or bike ride from Kerteminde
About 5 km south-west of Kerteminde

places.name: Middelfart & the Little Belt
places.summary: A small town on the Little Belt at the western edge of Funen, by the 1935 Old Little Belt Bridge, which you can climb on guided bridge walks. Porpoise-spotting boat trips leave from the harbour.
facts: Bridge walks across the girders are guided and booked in advance
Easy stop when driving between Funen and Jutland
Coastal path through Hindsgavl peninsula west of town

places.name: Langeland
places.summary: A long, thin rural island east of Tåsinge with the pretty town of Rudkøbing, Tranekær Castle, wild horses at Gulstav and a Cold War fortress at its southern tip.
facts: Linked by bridges to Tåsinge and Funen; no ferry needed
Langelandsfort is a Cold War museum with a submarine
Southern tip (Dovns Klint, Gulstav) is good for birdwatching in autumn migration

places.name: Rønne
places.summary: Bornholm's main town and ferry port, with cobbled lanes of low colourful houses around the old church. Practical base with the most accommodation and car hire.
facts: Ferries from Ystad (Sweden, ~80 min) and overnight from Køge arrive here
Car hire and the island bus network start here; a bike is a fine alternative
Bornholm's Museum covers island history

places.name: Hammershus
places.summary: The largest medieval castle ruin in Northern Europe, spread along a cliff above the sea at the north-western tip of Bornholm. A striking visitor centre and coastal paths make it a must.
facts: Free entry, open all hours; paid parking
The visitor centre has toilets, a café and exhibits
Walk on along the coast to Hammeren and Hammer Lighthouse

places.name: Hammeren coastal walk
places.summary: A granite headland at Bornholm's northern tip, ringed by a cliff path with sea views, the Hammer Odde lighthouse and the quarry lake Opalsøen. Combines naturally with Hammershus.
facts: Free; loop from Sandvig or Hammershus about 8–10 km
Opalsøen quarry lake is a popular swim spot
Rocky paths: wear proper shoes

places.name: Gudhjem
places.summary: A steep fishing village of half-timbered houses tumbling down to a tiny harbour, famous for its smokehouses and 'Sol over Gudhjem' smoked herring. Boats leave here for Christiansø.
facts: Eat smoked herring at one of the harbour smokehouses
Steep streets and little parking in summer: park at the top
Coast path south to Helligdommen and the art museum (about 5 km)

places.name: Østerlars Church
places.summary: The largest and most famous of Bornholm's four round churches, a fortified 12th-century church with buttresses, a central pillar decorated with frescoes and a lookout floor once used against raiders.
facts: Small entry fee
Nylars, Olsker and Nyker are the other round churches
Bornholm's Medieval Centre is a couple of kilometres away

places.name: Bornholm Art Museum
places.summary: A light-filled museum on the cliffs at Helligdommen showing the Bornholm painters and modern Danish art, with a path down to sea-carved granite rock formations.
facts: Ticketed; closed Mondays outside summer
Combine with the coastal path to Gudhjem
Free parking at the museum

places.name: Svaneke
places.summary: Denmark's easternmost town, a carefully preserved red-roofed harbour village known for its brewery, caramel and chocolate makers, glassblowers and smokehouse.
facts: Summer weekend market; small craft shops all year
Swim off the rocks at the harbour
Good stop between Gudhjem and Dueodde

places.name: Christiansø
places.summary: A tiny fortified island in the Ertholmene archipelago, an hour's boat ride from Gudhjem, with 17th-century naval fortifications, a handful of residents and huge colonies of eider ducks and guillemots.
facts: Day trips by boat from Gudhjem (and Allinge) most of the year; book in summer
No cars or pets; the whole island is a protected heritage site
Pack a picnic; there are only a couple of places to eat
places.caution: Crossings are cancelled in rough weather; check the day before.

places.name: Almindingen forest
places.summary: One of Denmark's largest forests in the middle of Bornholm, with rocky rift valleys like Ekkodalen, a lookout tower on Rytterknægten and a herd of European bison.
facts: Free; marked trails and bike paths from several car parks
The bison enclosure has a viewing platform and short walk
Ekkodalen is the most popular trail

places.name: Nexø
places.summary: Bornholm's second town and fishing port on the east coast, rebuilt after Soviet bombing in 1945. Useful for supplies and the nearby Paradisbakkerne hills.
facts: Paradisbakkerne, a rocky heath with marked trails, is just inland
Nexø Museum covers the 1945 liberation story
Bus routes link Nexø with Rønne, Svaneke and Dueodde

places.name: Dueodde Beach
places.summary: Bornholm's southern tip, a vast beach of extremely fine white sand backed by dunes and pine forest, with Denmark's tallest lighthouse.
facts: Free; paid parking near the lighthouse
Shallow, sandy water ideal for children
Climb the lighthouse in summer for the view
